% ============================================================ 2. motivation
\begin{frame}{Ordering is not deployment validity}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      Learning components now sit inside satellite communication software:
      correcting a propagated orbit, adapting a link parameter, gating a learned branch.

      \vspace{0.8em}
      Because these systems are temporal, we evaluate with a chronological split.
      That is necessary, and the conditions under which it is valid are well established.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The claim of this paper}
        It is \alert{not sufficient} --- and the gap is one of \emph{kind}, not degree.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.4em}
      \small A passing split can coexist with a deployment claim that was never checkable
      from the data in hand.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Train on the past, test on the future --- and still be unable to say the experiment was valid.}
\end{frame}

  \vspace{-0.3em}

% ============================================================ 4. core insight
\begin{frame}{The pivot: some validity is relational}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \begin{center}\input{figures/fig_relational.tex}\end{center}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \msg{\textbf{Row-local} validity is decidable from one realised run.
       \textbf{Relational} validity needs a second execution, a second source state,
       or a second aggregation level.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 5. method overview
\begin{frame}{Orbit-Evidence: validity as an executable contract}
  \vspace{-0.4em}
  \begin{center}\input{figures/fig_arch.tex}\end{center}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \only<1>{\msg{The experiment acts at $t_d$ from state it already holds.}}
  \only<2>{\msg{\Nrules{} executable rules in four layers observe it --- most inspect a single execution.}}
  \only<3>{\msg{Two cannot: the relational checks compare executions, or aggregation levels.}}
  \only<4>{\msg{A design that cannot support a decision returns \textsc{indeterminate} --- never \textsc{pass}.}}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 6. two key ideas
\begin{frame}{The two relational checks}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{L4.6 --- differential provenance}
        Two runs, identical manifest hash, \alert{different output}
        $\Rightarrow$ the manifest is incomplete.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.3em}
      \small
      Falsifies incompleteness \emph{without enumerating} the dependencies a manifest might omit.
      One-sided by construction: failure is a counterexample, success is not a certificate.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{L4.7 --- statistical-unit adequacy}
        Does dependence survive \alert{one declared level coarser}?
        Referenced to a permutation null.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.3em}
      \small
      And it \emph{abstains}: below four coarser groups the smallest reachable
      $p$ is $1/15 = 0.067 > \alpha$, so no such design could reject at all.
      That is an \emph{attainability} floor, not a power floor.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{One judgement generates both: neither obligation can be certified,
       so we accept checks that can only \emph{refuse}.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 8. real satellite evidence
\begin{frame}{Does the unit problem exist in real catalogue data?}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \centering
      \begin{tikzpicture}[x=1mm,y=1mm,font=\scriptsize,>={Latex[length=1.4mm]},
        n/.style={draw=black!55,line width=0.6pt,fill=blue!5,minimum width=24mm,
                  minimum height=6.5mm,align=center,inner sep=0.6mm}]
        \node[n] (p) at (0,26) {\Npasses{} visible passes};
        \node[n] (e) at (0,13) {\Nelsets{} element sets};
        \node[n] (o) at (0, 0) {\Nobjects{} objects};
        \draw[->,line width=0.7pt,black!70] (p) -- (e);
        \draw[->,line width=0.7pt,black!70] (e) -- (o);
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=oewarn,anchor=west,align=left] at (15,19.5)
          {$\hat{\rho}=\Naticc$\\$p=\Natp$\\\textbf{HALT}};
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!60,anchor=west,align=left] at (15,6.5)
          {$\hat{\rho}=\Naticcelset$\\\textbf{HALT}};
      \end{tikzpicture}
      \vspace{0.2em}

      {\scriptsize Observable: the \emph{in-track update increment} between consecutive fits.}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{What this means}\\[0.2em]
      \small Exchangeability of samples sharing a generating element set is
      \alert{rejected} --- one-sided lower bound $\Natlo$. The element set is not exchangeable
      either: \emph{no level tested here is}.\normalsize

      \vspace{0.5em}
      \textbf{What it does not mean}\\[0.2em]
      \small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1em}
        \item Not truth error --- an \emph{update increment} between fits sharing an
              observation arc, median $\Natmedian$\,km.
        \item Not a universal unit: the rule adjudicates the level it is \emph{given}.
        \item Not every observable: on elevation the same rule returned $\hat{\rho}=0.000$.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{Pre-registered intervention on the L4.1 halt}
        {\small Correcting \emph{only} the overlap: \textbf{HALT $\rightarrow$ PASS}, and the
        selected checkpoint changes in \alert{\Nconschanged{} of \Nconsseeds{}} paired seeds ---
        reproducible bit-for-bit.}
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.25em}
      \small The downstream metric moved on three seeds, \emph{in both directions}. Not a null:

      \vspace{0.3em}
      $\Rightarrow$ \textbf{not estimable} at the available paired-run resolution --- a

      nor about improving anomaly detection.}

% ============================================================ 10. what is new
\begin{frame}{What is actually new}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Not the primitives.}\\[0.3em]
      \small ICC(1), permutation inference, metamorphic relations, hermetic build closure,
      mutation testing --- all established, none proposed here.\normalsize

      \vspace{0.6em}
      \textbf{Not a checklist.}\\[0.3em]
      \small The \Nrules{} rules are the satellite \emph{instantiation}, not the
      contribution.\normalsize
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The method is the conversion}
        {\small
        \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.25em}
          \item Identify which validity obligations are \emph{relational}.
          \item Choose the counterfactual execution or coarser level that makes each
                \emph{falsifiable}.
          \item Encode the invariant as a contract --- and let an undecidable case return
                \textsc{indeterminate} rather than pass.
        \end{enumerate}}
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.2em}
      {\small A permutation reference is ordinarily an analysis step. Here it calibrates a
      \emph{gate} --- with an operating characteristic, and an abstention state.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 11. limitations
\begin{frame}{What this does not establish}
  \vspace{0.2em}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      {\small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.5em}
        \item \textbf{No completeness claim.} L4.6 is bounded by the caller's variation set;
              the input nobody thought of is absent by construction.
        \item \textbf{No RF or packet-level result.} The object of study is the experiment,
              not the link.
        \item \textbf{No improvement in learned accuracy.} The contract refuses claims;
              it does not make models better.
      \end{itemize}}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      {\small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.5em}
        \item \textbf{Curated faults are regression evidence.} Faults and rules largely share an
              origin, so $\Nfaults/\Nfaults$ measures \emph{reachability};
              \Nred{} of \Nrules{} rules have a demonstrated red fixture.
        \item \textbf{One third-party artifact, one channel.} It partially breaks the loop.
              It does not close it.
        \item \textbf{PASS means not rejected}, never verified.
      \end{itemize}}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Stated because a validity paper that overstates its own evidence has refuted itself.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ 12. takeaway
\begin{frame}[standout]
  Chronological separation remains necessary.\\
  It is not sufficient.

  \vspace{0.9em}
  {\normalsize\normalfont
  Some assumptions must become \textbf{executable}, \textbf{falsifiable},\\
  and allowed to \textbf{refuse} an unsupported claim.}
\end{frame}

% ============================================================ backup
\appendix

\begin{frame}{Backup --- why the abstention floor is not a power floor}
  % NOT {\small ...}: beamer reads a brace group at the start of a frame body as the SUBTITLE
  % argument, so the whole slide silently vanished. Set the size without a group.
  \small
  Three coarser groups of two units admit only $6!/(2!^{3}3!) = 15$ distinct assignments.
  The smallest reachable $p$ is $1/15 = 0.067 > \alpha$: \emph{no} design that small can reject
  at the nominal level, at any effect size.

  \vspace{0.6em}
  Four groups of two admit $105$, whose exhaustive reference reaches $0.0095$.

  \vspace{0.8em}
  So \textsc{indeterminate} is a statement about the \emph{design's resolution}, not about the
  strength of the effect. Collapsing it into \textsc{pass} is how a design that could not have
  rejected comes to look like one that did not.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- reproduction and provenance}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.4em}
    \item \texttt{make gate} regenerates the fault matrix and L4.7's operating characteristic,
          and \emph{refuses to build} if a headline number disagrees with the artifact at the
          sentence claiming it. 64 numbers are bound this way --- including every number on
          these slides.
    \item The two external studies are hash-verified rather than regenerated: their inputs do
          not ship.
    \item \texttt{make external-consequence-verify} checks the committed third-party results
          against the frozen commit, the frozen detector hash and the recorded data hashes ---
          16 checks, no training.
    \item The telemetry arrays came from a \emph{checksum-verified mirror} after the upstream
          endpoint became unavailable; per-file hashes matched two independently published
          checksum sources. That is mirror concordance, \emph{not} verification by the original
          publisher.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
